newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN chief says TV news needs more analysis.
newsitem.headline: UN chief says TV news needs more analysis.

text.p: Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali said on Thursday the immediacy and emotional power of television news should be used to ensure a better understanding of world events.
"Very often, news coverage is understood as a series of brief images of high dramatic intensity," he said.

"However, the risk there is to create a culture of the moment, a series of instantaneous reactions, without the analysis and the debate necessary to understand the many complex dimensions of various problems."

He was addressing the opening session of a two-day U.N. world television forum, focusing on the global role of television, organised jointly by the Italian Foreign Ministry and Radiotelevisione Italiana (RAI), that country's public broadcasting company.

Boutros-Ghali told the gathering, attended by broadcast personalities from scores of countries: "Quantity of information has too often been emphasised at the expense of quality of analysis. And technological advance has outpaced the capacity of national governments and international organisations to define, recognise and protect the public interest."
The challenge was "to harness the immediacy and emotional power of television in the service of greater knowledge and understanding of world events," he said.
"The cultural, economic and political impact of media globalization demands an informed and considered response from us all."
Decisions about which stories to cover, and for how long, had a real and lasting impact on the course of international events, he told the forum.

Referring to stark television footage of mass starvation in Africa and of war in the Balkans, he said: "Whether in Ethiopia in 1984 or Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1994, television has had -- and will have -- a vital role in focus world attention on the need for urgent action and a swift international response."
